propositions: T5c security findings lack grounding in the current codebase and configuration; 46% cite repo artifacts despite an as-written evaluation stance, and 30% are undeclared-access-posture template findings that Pass-2 cannot drop, leading to duplicative findings (99 reviews with ≥2 same-shape findings) and displacement of other criteria in 103 advisory-cap-limited reviews.

The rubric must add a criterion-local GROUNDING OVERRIDE directing evaluation against the current codebase and configuration, where a control defined elsewhere flips a finding, to disambiguate security implications from spec text alone.

Undeclared-access-posture findings must be deduplicated at source to emit at most ONE per plan, with additional surfaces folded into that finding's evidence rather than generating one finding per surface.

Candidate findings citing neither a read repo artifact nor a quoted plan sentence must be demoted to minor severity (never suppressed) to prevent ungrounded findings from reaching the blocking threshold.

Only two HIGH-severity classes warrant blocking: plaintext secrets on boundary-crossing paths and undeclared internet-reachable sensitive surfaces; all other findings must be capped at minor severity.

The T5c routing entry must shift from advisory @ 0.95 to blocking @ 0.9 to enable blocking on grounded, high-confidence findings while the rubric text levers prevent non-HIGH findings from reaching the threshold.
